parole.testo: Corruption of Sicilian/Italian capatosta, meaning "stubborn", "with a thick skull", used in Italian-American English.
Likely from Sicilian la bonza (“any large rounded liquid container”) or Sicilian la panza (“the belly”).

parole.significato: A silver coin in ancient Sicily, worth one fifth of a drachm.
parole.testo: From Sicilian, from Medieval Latin litra, from Ancient Greek λίτρα (lítra). Doublet of arratel, libbra, Libra, libra, lira, litre, livre, and rottol.

parole.significato: Luvarus imperialis, a large ellipsoidal perciform fish related to the surgeonfish.

parole.testo: From Sicilian malocchiu. Doublet of malocchio.

parole.significato: A type of Sicilian sesame bread.
parole.testo: From Sicilian, diminutive of muffe (“mold, mushroom”), perhaps due to the appearance of the round sandwich bread being reminiscent of a mushroom cap.

parole.significato: A variety of ice cream (or, formerly, other confection) that contains chopped candied fruit.
parole.testo: From Sicilian tutti frutti (“all fruits”), so attested in 1838 for a kind of sorbet.
Adapted from Sicilian vâ fa' 'n culu. Akin to Italian vaffanculo.
